rows.notes: `containing` is not a minijinja 2.16.0 test at all; the Go port shipped it. The engine must reject it rather than the fork answering true.
`cycler` is a Go-port global the engine does not have.
`joiner` is a Go-port global the engine does not have.
`lipsum` is a Go-port global the engine does not have.
The map form of the withdrawn urlencode filter, which the upstream Go corpus also exercised. Both spellings must be rejected.
The engine's Cow<str> argument stringifies a non-string, so this is not a type error.
none stringifies to `none`, so this renders NONE rather than an empty string.
An empty pattern matches at every character boundary in both engines.
minijinja's replace takes exactly two arguments. Jinja2's optional count is not part of it, and the Go port accepted it; a third argument must be an error.
Rust's str::trim is Unicode-aware; a Go cutset of four ASCII bytes is not.
Rust's str::split with an empty pattern yields leading and trailing empty pieces; Go's strings.Split does not.
split takes Arc<str>, which requires a real string, unlike the casing filters.
str::lines produces no empty final line for a trailing newline.
A lone carriage return is not a line break for str::lines.
Rust's parse::<i128> rejects a leading space; a lenient Go parser would not.
Rust's f64 parser accepts inf/nan spellings.
minijinja compares strings case-insensitively via unicase unless told otherwise.
The stock engine's sum rejects a non-number. BAML replaces this filter in its own environment; that is the deferred profile, not this one.
serde_json escapes < > & as \u003c and friends here; Go's encoding/json has its own HTML-escaping rules.
An empty argument list is not an argument.
A division by zero inside a test; the parked work recorded a hang in this area.
U+2170 has the Lowercase property but is not category Ll, so Go's unicode.IsLower and Rust's char::is_lowercase disagree about it.

rows.notes: debug() with an argument renders the value's repr, which is comparable. The no-argument form dumps the whole environment in Rust's Debug format, type paths and all, and is deliberately not pinned byte for byte.
The state dump is not byte-comparable, but its presence is.
The sharp s in the middle of a word, so the expansion is not at a boundary.
Full case mapping: lowercases to i plus a combining dot above.
A capital sigma at the end of a word lowercases to the final form.
A combining acute is case-ignorable, so the sigma is still word final.
Every ASCII punctuation starts a new word in the engine.
Length counts characters, and an astral character is one.
minijinja's lexer has no \U escape and rejects the literal outright; the Go port's lexer accepts Go-style escapes. A lexer difference, not a builtin one.
Nor does it have Rust's \u{...} form.
It does have \x, and the Go port agrees.
A modifier letter has the Lowercase property but is category Lm.
A superscript two is Unicode-numeric but not a decimal digit.
A combining Greek ypogegrammeni is Other_Alphabetic: Rust says alphabetic, Go's unicode.IsLetter does not.
Unlike the `replace` filter, the Python method does take a count.
find returns a BYTE offset in the engine, so a two-byte first character shifts it.
Without an unknown-method callback the engine reports an unknown method. The fork must produce the same category rather than an unknown-function error.
An existing non-callable attribute is an invalid operation, not an unknown method.
